faq.a: Ababil is associated with the Arabic form أبابيل, whose core sense is flocks, swarms (in bands).

faq.q: What is the origin of Ababil?
faq.a: Ababil is associated with Arabic. Abābīl occurs only in Sūrat al-Fīl and means 'flocks in bands'; it is plural with no singular. The source record's gloss 'Rain from the sky' is unsupported.
Yes — the underlying form أبابيل is Arabic.
Ababil can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.

Ababil should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. أبابيل occurs in the Qur'an (Sūrat al-Fīl 105:3) as a common noun meaning 'flocks, swarms'; it is not a Qur'anic proper name

faq.q: What does Ababil mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Ababil is rendered ابابیل and carries the sense جھنڈ، غول.

faq.a: Romanization variants include Ababil, ababil. Script forms are أبابيل, ابابيل, ابابیل, अबाबील.

faq.q: Is Ababil a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as unisex. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
